scope: Three pre-registered active or volatile official documentation/specification URLs for incremental embedding updates, blue-green deployment and provenance modeling; no source discovery was performed.

verified_claims: Qdrant documents deriving a content fingerprint such as SHA-256 and a deterministic point ID from a chunk's source position.
Its incremental-update pattern leaves unchanged chunks untouched, re-embeds changed text, reuses vectors when content moves, adds new text and deletes text absent from the current source list.
The tutorial explicitly notes that its simple implementation re-reads the whole collection and becomes costly at large scale because of full scans and request-size limits.
records.boundary: This is a Qdrant tutorial pattern that assumes deterministic chunking and an inexpensive current-source enumeration. Hashing and ID design do not alone guarantee synchronization, and scale limits require workload-specific architecture.

verified_claims: Qdrant documents blue-green cluster deployment with a validation period before switching application traffic to the green endpoint.
The guide recommends retaining a snapshot as a rollback point and describes switching back to the blue endpoint or restoring from a snapshot if rollback is needed.
It identifies the temporary cost of running two clusters and advises completing green-cluster testing before decommissioning blue.
records.boundary: This is Qdrant operational guidance, not a universal zero-downtime or recovery guarantee. Snapshot validity, traffic cutover, data freshness and rollback timing require deployment-specific drills.

verified_claims: W3C PROV-O defines an ontology for representing provenance with core classes prov:Entity, prov:Activity and prov:Agent.
The recommendation defines relationships including wasGeneratedBy, wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo, used and wasAssociatedWith for tracing origin, derivation and activity context.
W3C identifies PROV-O as a stable recommendation suitable for reference and citation, while separating the ontology from application-specific storage and exchange implementations.
records.boundary: PROV-O is a provenance vocabulary, not an automatic lineage collector or RAG-specific schema. Implementations must define identifiers, retention, privacy and event completeness for their system.
